gaps.summary: Native generation checkpoint/tail recovery and disk-backed permanent command lookup are implemented with lineage-sealed active tails and explicit downgrade export.
gaps.disposition: CLOSED. Canonical native startup consumes a digest-bound selected generation, bounded hot replay and the lineage-bound active tail instead of repopulating all historical commands into the coordinator. Historical `(agent, session, command)` identity and canonical request hashes remain in pinned cumulative disk indexes used by status/admission lookup; send-attempt history is merged across the cut and index corruption fails closed. V2 stopped-state maintenance fsyncs immutable delta generations, atomically rotates the active path to a non-JSON lineage sentinel, binds parent manifests and current pointers by SHA-256, and preserves V1 reading for upgrade. Tests cover repeated generations, bounded active-tail growth, publication crash boundaries, ancient same-ID duplicate/conflict, native restart without a second venue send, send-attempt continuity, current/parent/sentinel corruption rejection, V1-to-V2 upgrade and create-only strict legacy JSONL export for downgrade. No command identity is expired, no journal history is deleted, and PAPER/LIVE authorization remains false.

Callback lag, callback conflict, quote/snapshot age, Broker reconciliation duration and network-policy producers remain absent with explicit presence=false rather than synthetic zero. No target-host SLO or real notification is proven.

gaps.summary: Actual target-host multiday stability, failure collection and delivery to the real operator remain unverified.
gaps.disposition: Split from the external operations portion of OMS-LIFECYCLE-002 without claiming completion. Disposable PID1, multi-UID process fixtures and loopback monitoring are independent source evidence, not an activated target-host collector or a real receiver.
